subject: Clarify metered-to-seat wrap and channel waterfall for AWS private offer
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@vertica.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating private offer packaging + channel margin question

Hi Mina —

Thanks for taking this. Quick intro: I'm Sara (procurement) at VerticaAI. We're evaluating Redwood's AWS private offer for an upcoming initiative — roughly 500k expected spend in year one across inference and embeddings. Our procurement team prefers a hybrid packaging (metered + seat wrap) to simplify downstream billing to our customers, but we have to ensure reseller margins and list-price anchoring line up with our marketplace distributor requirements.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood supports a seat-wrapped metered SKU (single private-offer SKU that bills meter but shows as a seat license on our side)
- Typical anchor/list-price guidance when offering a committed private offer vs hosted list price
- How reseller margins would be handled — we need a waterfall for reseller pass-through (example: 10% broker, 7% distributor, 8% reseller) and whether Redwood can provide an ops-friendly invoice path

I've attached our internal requirements (vertica_requirements.xlsx) that outline expected consumption profiles and a preferred billing cadence. If you can send a quick packaging proposal and high-level margin mapping we'll share with our procurement/legal.

Appreciate it — can we aim for a short sync later this week?

Best,
Sara
Sara Liu
Procurement Lead — VerticaAI
Attachment: vertica_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@vertica.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating private offer packaging + channel margin question

Sara —

Thanks, and great to meet you (virtually). We can absolutely support the pattern you're describing (metered runtime under a seat-wrapped private-offer SKU). Two quick paths we typically propose depending on billing/contract preferences:

Option A — Committed Meter + Seat Wrap (recommended)
- Create a single private-offer SKU that Redwood meters per-token for inference and embeddings but maps to a seat license in your billing system.
- Anchor/list price: set private-offer list at ~25–35% below public list depending on commit term/volume; published list price remains the canonical reference for reseller commissions.
- Channel waterfall: we can output invoice splits and pass-through entries at invoice time; typical structure (example) is broker 8–12% -> distributor 5–8% -> reseller 6–10% depending on nested agreements.

Option B — Dual SKU (explicit seat + metered add-on)
- Seat license SKU for entitlement + separate metered SKU for consumption. Cleaner for accounting if the distributor requires distinct line items, but slightly more operational overhead to reconcile usage.

Attached is a short proposed_packaging_v1.pdf with a recommended mapping and a draft DocuSign PO we can pre-fill to speed procurement. A couple of asks so we can finalize the waterfall and pricing anchor:
1) Confirm preferred billing display (single seat line item vs two-line item)
2) Confirm expected monthly peak TPS / token volume (the workbook helps here)
3) Any distributor constraints (minimum list price floor, commission caps)

If you like, I can route a one-pager and the three-option margin waterfall to our reseller/ops team and loop in Ben (channel ops) for the invoice path. I'm free Thu 10–11am PT for a 30 min sync — does that work?

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_packaging_v1.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: draft_DocuSign_PO.pdf (pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evaluating private offer packaging + channel margin question

Ben / Irene —

Looping you in on VerticaAI (attached requirements). They're targeting a ~500k Y1 private offer on AWS and want a metered-to-seat wrap so the integrator shows a single seat license. Key asks:
- Confirmation we can produce an invoice with pass-through waterfall entries (broker/distributor/reseller) and maintain list-price anchoring for commission calculations.
- Recommended anchor discount band for a 12-month commit (they indicated ~500k). In the past we've done 25–35% off public list but want ops to validate whether we can push tighter with a conditional early-adopter credit.
- Any ops constraints if we do Option A (single SKU mapping) vs Option B (dual SKU) — especially around billing reconciliation for the distributor.

I've attached my proposed_packaging_v1.pdf — it's intentionally opinionated. If you can review and send back a succinct margin-waterfall snippet (numbers we can share with the buyer) I'll move to a call with them. Finance sign-off will be required for the final anchor.

Thanks — cc'ing Sara in case she has follow-up.

Mina

Attachment: proposed_packaging_v1.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: vertica_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evaluating private offer packaging + channel margin question

Mina —

Quick read: we can support Option A for invoice presentation; ops will emit usage lines + a seat-wrapped entitlement reference. High-level margin waterfall I recommend sharing with Vertica (example numbers, illustrative):
- Broker: 10% (applied to published list price)
- Distributor: 6% (applied after broker)
- Reseller: 8% (final downstream margin)

Recommended public-list anchor guidance for a 12mo / $500k committal: private-offer list = public_list * 0.72 (i.e., 28% off) with an early-adopter credit of 5% applied in month 1–3 that is reclaimed across months 10–12 if commit velocity meets ramp targets. That keeps effective discount within the 25–35% window but preserves list-floor for commission calculations.

Ops constraints: single-SKU mapping increases reconciliation work by ~1 FTE-month in the first quarter for the distributor (we can build an automated extract but timeline is ~3 weeks). If the buyer prefers lower ops lift, recommend Option B.

If this looks fine, I'll draft a short margin-waterfall note and send to Sara + finance for quick sign-off.

Ben
Senior Channel Ops — Redwood Inference
